doc.title: Rashied Ali and Henry Grimes interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 30, 2009

title: Rhythm and blues bands and Granoff
summary: Ali played with Lin Holt, Dick Hart and the Heartaches, and Big Maybelle, and briefly attended Granoff.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: But then you both got into the rhythm & blues scene. And I’m trying to get a sense of the guys you played with: Big Maybelle and so forth. Those were current pop artists at the time, in those years, right.

Yeah, the Philadelphia based artists, I mean, most of them they were all out of Philadelphia: Lin Holt and he played saxophone, and actually Trane played with Lin Holt. And that was great. I got that gig with him just for a little while. And Dick Hart and the Heartaches, I played with that band.

Dick Hart and the Heartaches, that’s what they called themselves. And Big Maybelle, I played with her for a couple of jobs. And I mean you know, I mean that was the way to go. I mean that was actually, it was more or less my learning years playing with that kind of stuff. Because I always wanted to play bebop. That was my main goal. But there wasn’t that many gigs to get and I wasn’t all that really experienced to get those gigs yet, so I cut my teeth on playing with rhythm & blues bands for a while. And that was cool too, because what I liked about that was that Coltrane was always my idol, after seeing him with Miles Davis, and then when I look back on it, I had noticed that he had played with a lot of those bands at first, you know, when he first came through. And he also went to Granoff. So when I came out of the Army I enrolled in Granoff Music School. But that was only for a half a semester before I just got out of there. I didn’t really like dealing with theory and all that kind of stuff, I really wanted to play. But I just went there because that was the place where all I thought all the bad musicians went to. So I played a lot of good rhythm & blues stuff for a while. Then I just started playing jazz.
